targetArchitecture.runtime: Browser -> Vercel -> Firebase Auth token -> Render EOS API -> EOS authorization -> PostgreSQL
targetArchitecture.principle: Firebase is permitted only for sign-in identity and Firebase UID correlation to an EOS Principal/Employee. All business data, business authorization, and business transport must run through the Render EOS API against PostgreSQL, not through Firestore or Firebase Functions.

IDENTITY_ONLY.description: Firebase usage that establishes or verifies who the caller is (sign-in, ID token verification, custom-claims issuance) or correlates a Firebase UID to an EOS Principal/Employee. This is permanently permitted and is NOT part of the exit ratchet.

BUSINESS_RUNTIME.description: Firebase usage that transports, persists, authorizes, or executes EOS business logic: Firestore reads/writes, Firebase Functions callables/triggers, and firebase-admin Firestore persistence. Must trend to zero per the architecture ruling.

migrationStates.NOT_STARTED: No Render EOS API / PostgreSQL equivalent exists yet for this dependency.
migrationStates.DUAL_READ_TEST: A Render EOS API / PostgreSQL equivalent exists and is being verified against the Firebase path; Firebase remains the system of record.
migrationStates.READY: The Render EOS API / PostgreSQL equivalent has passed verification and cutover is authorized but not yet performed.
migrationStates.CUTOVER: The Render EOS API / PostgreSQL path is the system of record; the Firebase path is inert in the live runtime.
migrationStates.RETIRED: The Firebase business dependency has been removed from source and from the baseline.

dispositions.IDENTITY_ONLY: This dependency is sign-in identity or UID correlation and is retained permanently; it does not migrate.
dispositions.MIGRATE_TO_POSTGRES_RENDER: This dependency has (or will have) a live EOS business equivalent and must be re-pointed to the Render EOS API / PostgreSQL.
dispositions.ARCHIVE: This dependency serves data with no ongoing live business need; it is captured as read-only evidence/history rather than migrated forward.
dispositions.RETIRE: This dependency has no ongoing purpose and is deleted rather than migrated.

ratchet.rule: For every baselineKey listed under classification.BUSINESS_RUNTIME.baselineKeys, the set of live-runtime files depending on it may only shrink relative to docs/architecture/firebase-exit-baseline.json. It may never grow. A file already in the baseline for a given key is temporarily tolerated so migration can proceed incrementally; a file NOT in the baseline for that key introducing that dependency is a new violation.

domainMigrationWaveModel.description: Each baseline file belongs to exactly one domain: the first path segment beneath field-ops-app-vite/src or functions/src (for example functions/src/cycleCount/cycleCountCallables.ts belongs to domain 'cycleCount'). A migration wave groups one or more domains that move to the Render EOS API / PostgreSQL together. This manifest defines the model only -- it does not assign domains to waves, order waves, or assert a disposition per domain, because that scheduling decision belongs to the engineers and owners doing the migration work, not to this control document. Once a wave is scheduled, it is recorded here as an entry below with the domain names, its disposition (one of the values in `dispositions`), and its migrationState (one of the values in `migrationStates`).
